request: Which came first? Surprising pairs from history: tap the older one in each pair. #interactive #short
subtitle: The fax or the telephone? Oxford or the Aztecs? The pyramids or the last mammoths? Tap the older one, and watch history's timeline fold.

sources.title: Alexander Bain (inventor)
sources.finding: Bain received British patent 9745 for his 'electric printing telegraph', the first fax, on 27 May 1843; Bell's telephone patent came in 1876

sources.title: University of Oxford: history
sources.finding: there is no clear date of foundation, but teaching existed at Oxford in some form in 1096

sources.title: Temporal dynamics of woolly mammoth genome erosion prior to extinction (Cell)
sources.finding: the Wrangel Island mammoth population survived until about 4,000 years ago

commands.speak: Which came first? Three pairs, and in each one, history plays a trick on you.

ask.question: Which came first? In each pair, tap the one that is older.
ask.right: The fax, Oxford and the pyramid all came first.

feedback.good: History tricked you only a little.

commands.speak: First: the fax is older than the telephone.
Alexander Bain patented a way to send pictures by telegraph in 1843, thirty-three years before Bell's phone.
His design used two swinging pendulums, kept in step, to scan a picture line by line.
Next, Oxford was teaching students by 1096, more than two centuries before the Aztecs founded their capital, Tenochtitlan.
So when that city rose from its lake, Oxford had already been teaching for generations.
And the Great Pyramid is older than the last woolly mammoths.
The pyramid was finished around 2560 BC.
A small herd survived on Wrangel Island, in the Arctic Ocean, until about four thousand years ago.
So when the pyramid was already five centuries old, mammoths still walked the Earth.
